scope: Source inspection only; no Julia generation, hash, build or execution

sources.finding: Default library initialization parses options, resolves its image and bundle paths, then calls jl_init_with_image_file. This wrapper has no Julia expression-evaluation call; shutdown calls jl_atexit_hook.
The proposed direct driver's init_julia and shutdown_julia declarations agree with this header.
create_library accepts custom initialization C/header files and an image-build script. These are potential build-time configuration routes, not proof that an application is AOT.
The image-file entry preloads the selected image and invokes jl_init_.

The supplied-image branch restores the image. The separate no-image branch loads boot.jl. Startup initializes runtime facilities and runs the saved module initializer sequence after starting threads and enabling GC.
Module initialization resolves each module's __init__ and invokes it through jl_apply. Nested initializer behavior therefore still requires native coverage and observation.

remaining_evidence: Pin the actual PackageCompiler initializer/header and Julia runtime/image/header bytes under the common mutex.
Bind the exact produced library, C launcher, exported ABI and actual runtime option receipt.
Observe the complete loaded module initializer sequence and all threads from before initialization through shutdown.
Distinguish codegen target initialization or native-pointer lookup from actual Julia code emission; record unresolved hook semantics explicitly.
Reject actual interpreter and code-emission events using complete native routes and a missing-native-method negative canary.
Resolve binarytrees4 Main/package bindings without timed source evaluation or a changed distributed algorithm.
Preserve whole-process startup cost and use fresh matched derived JIT measurements alongside any qualified AOT measurements.
